questions.sampleA1:
My best friend is... Maria.

She is nice.

We play.
questions.sampleA2:
My best friend is Anna.

We go to school together and we play after school.

She is very funny and kind, and I like her very much.
questions.sampleB1:
My best friend is probably Sarah.

I've known her for about five years now.

We met at university and we have a lot in common.

I think she's a really good person and I can always talk to her about anything.

Sometimes we disagree, but we always work it out.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, that's a tough one, but I'd have to say it's Emily. We've known each other since school, so we go way back. The thing is, she's the one person I can properly open up to, and no matter what happens, she always has my back. I suppose what I value most is that I can be completely myself around her.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Mening eng yaqin do'stim... Mariya.

U yaxshi qiz.

Biz o'ynaymiz.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Mening eng yaqin do'stim Anna.

Biz birga maktabga boramiz va darsdan keyin o'ynaymiz.

U juda quvnoq va mehribon, va u menga juda yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Mening eng yaqin do'stim, ehtimol, Sara.

Men uni taxminan besh yildan beri bilaman.

Biz universitetda tanishganmiz va bizda ko'p umumiy narsalar bor.

Menimcha, u juda yaxshi inson va men har doim u bilan har qanday narsa haqida gaplasha olaman.

Ba'zan biz kelishmovchiliklarga duch kelamiz, lekin biz har doim buni hal qilamiz.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Bu qiyin savol, chunki mening bir nechta yaqin do'stlarim bor, lekin menimcha, eng yaxshi do'stim Emili bo'ladi.

Biz o'smirlik davridan beri do'stmiz va birgalikda juda ko'p narsalarni boshdan kechirdik.

U juda qo'llab-quvvatlovchi va tushunuvchan, va men bilaman, nima bo'lishidan qat'iy nazar, men har doim unga ishonishim mumkin.

Ish va oilaviy majburiyatlar tufayli biz avvalgidek tez-tez ko'rishmaymiz, lekin qachon ko'rishsak, go'yo vaqt o'tmagandek bo'ladi.

Oxir oqibat, men uning halolligini va uning yonida o'zimning asl shaxsim bo'la olishimni qadrlayman.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Who is your best friend?
idioms: a friend in need is a friend indeed - "do'st kulfatda bilinadi"
two peas in a pod - "bir olmaning ikki pallasi (juda o'xshash yoki doim birga yuradiganlar)"
through thick and thin - "yaxshi va yomon kunlarda"
phrases: thick and thin - "yaxshi va yomon kunlar (og'ir damlar)"
shoulder to cry on - "dardlashish(yig'lash) uchun yelka (hamdardlik bildiruvchi inson)"
sentenceStarters: "My best friend is someone I've known since childhood, and…" - "Mening eng yaqin do'stim — yoshligimdan beri biladigan va … insonimdir"
"Furthermore, we have supported each other through…" - "Bundan tashqari, biz bir-birimizni … qo'llab-quvvatlaganmiz"

questions.sampleAnswer:
My best friend is someone I've known since childhood, and we share an incredibly strong bond. We effortlessly understand each other, often knowing what the other is thinking without even saying a word.
Furthermore, we have supported each other through thick and thin. Whether I'm celebrating a success or going through a tough time, they are always a shoulder to cry on. "A friend in need is a friend indeed," and they have proven that time and again.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening eng yaqin do'stim - bolaligimdan beri tanigan odam, va bizning o'rtamizda nihoyatda kuchli aloqa bor. Biz bir-birimizni juda oson tushunamiz, ko'pincha bir-birimiz nima haqida o'ylayotganini bir og'iz so'z demasdan bilamiz.

Bundan tashqari, biz bir-birimizni yaxshi ham, yomon kunlarda ham qo'llab-quvvatlab kelganmiz. Men muvaffaqiyatni nishonlayotgan bo'lsam ham, qiyin kunlarni boshdan kechirayotgan bo'lsam ham, ular har doim yordam berishga tayyor. "Do'st dardingga sherik," deganlaridek, ular buni qayta-qayta isbotlashgan.

questions.prompt: Do you take vitamins or supplements?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I take vitamin. One vitamin. Every day.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I take vitamins. I take vitamin C because I get sick sometimes. And I want to be healthy. It's good for me, I think.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I do take some vitamins. I take vitamin D, especially in the winter, because I don't get much sun. I think it helps me feel better. Also, I sometimes take a multivitamin if I feel like my diet isn't very good.
questions.sampleB2: Yeah, I do, though I'm not too strict about it. To be honest, I mainly take vitamin D over the winter, since we get by on very little sunlight here. I've also started taking magnesium because I read it helps with sleep. That said, I try not to rely on pills — I reckon a balanced diet should really do the heavy lifting.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men vitamin qabul qilaman. Bir dona vitamin. Har kuni.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men vitaminlar qabul qilaman. Men vitamin C qabul qilaman, chunki ba'zida kasal bo'lib qolaman. Va men sog'lom bo'lishni xohlayman. Bu men uchun yaxshi, deb o'ylayman.
questions.uzSampleB1: Ha, men ba'zi vitaminlar qabul qilaman. Men D vitaminini, ayniqsa qishda qabul qilaman, chunki quyosh nurini unchalik olmayman. Menimcha, bu o'zimni yaxshiroq his qilishimga yordam beradi. Shuningdek, agar ovqatlanishim unchalik yaxshi emas deb his qilsam, ba'zan multivitamin ham qabul qilaman.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Ha, men vaqti-vaqti bilan qo'shimchalar qabul qilaman. Men bunga juda ham qat'iy rioya qilaman deb ayta olmayman, lekin quyosh nurining yetishmasligini qoplash uchun qish oylarida D vitaminini qabul qilaman. Shuningdek, ba'zan magniy ham qabul qilaman, chunki o'qiganlarimga ko'ra u uyquga yordam berishi mumkin.
Shunga qaramay, men har doim juda ko'p qabul qilishdan ehtiyot bo'laman, chunki menimcha, muvozanatli ovqatlanish asosiy ozuqa manbai bo'lishi kerak.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Do you take vitamins or supplements?
idioms: you are what you eat - "nimani yesangiz, o'sha sizsiz (sog'lom ovqat – sog'lom tana)"
an apple a day keeps the doctor away - "kuniga bitta olma shifokorni uzoqlashtiradi"
fit as a fiddle - "tep-tetik (sog'lom)"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I regularly take a daily multivitamin to ensure…" - "Ha, men … ta'minlash uchun muntazam ravishda kundalik multivitamin ichaman"
"However, I try not to solely rely on them. I believe that…" - "Biroq, men faqat ularga tayanmaslikka harakat qilaman. Men ishonamanki…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I regularly take a daily multivitamin to ensure my body gets all the essential nutrients it needs. Sometimes, my diet lacks certain elements, so supplements act as a safety net for my overall health.
However, I try not to solely rely on them. I believe that maintaining a balanced diet full of fresh fruits and vegetables is much more important. After all, "you are what you eat."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men tanam kerakli barcha muhim oziq moddalarni olishini ta'minlash uchun muntazam ravishda har kuni multivitamin qabul qilaman. Ba'zan, mening ovqatlanishimda ayrim elementlar yetishmaydi, shuning uchun qo'shimchalar umumiy salomatligim uchun xavfsizlik tarmog'i vazifasini o'taydi.

Biroq, men ularga faqatgina suyanmaslikka harakat qilaman. Menimcha, yangi meva va sabzavotlarga to'la muvozanatli ovqatlanishni saqlash ancha muhim. Axir, "nima yesang, shusan."

questions.sampleA1: Yes. I like my neighbours. They are nice. They say hello.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like my neighbours. They are friendly and we sometimes talk. They have a dog and I like the dog. But sometimes they are a little noisy.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I think I like my neighbours. They are mostly friendly and helpful. For example, they helped me when my car broke down. However, sometimes they have loud parties, which can be annoying. But overall, they are good neighbours.
questions.sampleB2: Yeah, on the whole I get on really well with them. We're not exactly best mates, but we're on friendly terms — we'll stop for a quick chat, and they'll keep an eye on my place when I'm away. Every now and then there's a bit of noise, but honestly, nothing worth kicking up a fuss about. There's a nice sense of community on our street.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men qo'shnilarimni yaxshi ko'raman. Ular yaxshi odamlar. Ular salomlashadi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men qo'shnilarimni yaxshi ko'raman. Ular do'stona va biz ba'zan gaplashamiz. Ularning iti bor va menga it yoqadi. Lekin ba'zan ular biroz shovqinli bo'lishadi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men qo'shnilarimni yaxshi ko'raman deb o'ylayman. Ular asosan do'stona va yordam berishga tayyor.
Masalan, mashinam buzilib qolganda ular menga yordam berishdi.
Biroq, ba'zida ular shovqinli bazmlar o'tkazishadi, bu esa bezovta qilishi mumkin.
Lekin umuman olganda, ular yaxshi qo'shnilar.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ko'p jihatdan, qo'shnilarim bilan ijobiy munosabatda ekanligimni aytishim mumkin. Ular odatda e'tiborli va biz tez-tez xushmuomalalik qilamiz. Agar men uzoqda bo'lsam, ular mening pochtamni yig'ishtirib olishadi va men ham ular uchun shunday qilaman. Biz ayniqsa yaqin do'stlar bo'lmasak ham, jamoatchilik hissi va o'zaro hurmat bor. Ba'zida, ba'zi kichik shovqin muammolari bo'lishi mumkin, ammo bu mahallaning umumiy tinch muhitini buzadigan darajada ahamiyatli emas.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you like your neighbours?
idioms: good fences make good neighbors - "yaxshi to'siqlar maza qo'shnilar yaratadi (shaxsiy hududni hurmat qilish yaxshi munosabatlar garovi)"
keep an eye on - "ko'z quloq bo'lib turmoq"
close to home - "uyga yaqin / yurakka yaqin"
sentenceStarters: "Generally speaking, I have a very amicable relationship with…" - "Umuman olganda, mening … bilan juda do'stona munosabatim bor"
"Fortunately, they are very quiet and respectful of boundaries, which…" - "Yaxshiyamki, ular juda tinch va shaxsiy chegaralarni hurmat qilishadi, bu esa…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Generally speaking, I have a very amicable relationship with my neighbors. We frequently exchange greetings and help each other out with small favors, like collecting mail or keeping an eye on the house while one of us is away.
Fortunately, they are very quiet and respectful of boundaries, which creates a peaceful living environment. It’s always nice to have people nearby you can rely on, showing that "good fences make good neighbors" when respect is mutual.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Umuman olganda, men qo'shnilarim bilan juda do'stona munosabatdaman. Biz tez-tez salomlashamiz va bir-birimizga mayda yordamlar beramiz, masalan, pochta yig'ish yoki birimiz yo'qligida uyga ko'z-quloq bo'lish.

Yaxshiyamki, ular juda sokin va chegaralarni hurmat qilishadi, bu esa tinch yashash muhitini yaratadi. Yaqiningizda ishonishingiz mumkin bo'lgan odamlarning bo'lishi har doim yaxshi, bu o'zaro hurmat bo'lganda "yaxshi devorlar yaxshi qo'shnilarni yaratadi" degan maqolni isbotlaydi.

questions.sampleA2: I see friends in the picture. They are talking and drinking. It looks nice and they are happy.
questions.sampleB1: In the first picture, there are some friends. They are together and talking. I think they are having fun. However, in the other picture, there are only two people.
questions.sampleB2: So, in the first picture, there's a group of about five friends gathered round a café table, and they're all laughing away over coffee and cake. It looks really lively — a proper social get-together. The second one, on the other hand, is much more low-key and intimate, showing just two guys sitting outside with takeaway coffees. One's gesturing with both hands, so they seem to be deep in conversation. To me, the first captures the buzz of a big group, while the second feels like a proper heart-to-heart.
questions.uzSampleA2: Rasmda do'stlarni ko'ryapman. Ular gaplashishyapti va ichishyapti. Yaxshi ko'rinadi va ular baxtli.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Birinchi rasmda bir nechta do'stlar bor. Ular birga va gaplashishyapti. Menimcha, ular xursandchilik qilishyapti.
Lekin, boshqa rasmda faqat ikki kishi bor.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Birinchi rasmda bir guruh do'stlar tasvirlangan, ehtimol ziyofatda yoki yig'ilishda. Ular xursand bo'lib, kulishib, gaplashishayotganga o'xshaydi. Bu jonli va ijtimoiy muhitga o'xshaydi.

Ikkinchi rasm boshqacha; unda faqat ikki do'st bor. Ular bir-biriga yaqin o'tirishibdi, ehtimol shaxsiy suhbatlashishayotgandir. Bu yanada samimiy va jiddiy munosabatni ko'rsatadi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - Describe the pictures
idioms: a heart-to-heart - "dildan suhbat"
the life of the party - "davra nuri (davrani qizituvchi odam)"
two's company, three's a crowd - "ikki kishi - davra, uch kishi - olomon (ba'zan ikkita odamning birga bo'lishi qulayroq ekanligini bildiradi)"
sentenceStarters: "The first picture depicts a larger group of friends…" - "Birinchi rasmda kattaroq do'stlar guruhi tasvirlangan…"
"In contrast, the second picture highlights a much more…" - "Aksincha, ikkinchi rasmda ancha … alohida ta'kidlangan"

questions.sampleAnswer:
The first picture depicts a larger group of friends casually hanging out around a table. They are deeply engaged in conversation, laughing, and clearly enjoying a very vibrant social gathering. It looks like a fun, lighthearted group dynamic.
In contrast, the second picture highlights a much more intimate setting with only two friends having coffee. They are leaning in, maintaining direct eye contact, which suggests they are having a deep, meaningul discussion or perhaps sharing personal advice. It feels much calmer and more focused than the first picture.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasmda bir guruh do'stlar stol atrofida bemalol o'tirgani tasvirlangan. Ular suhbatga chuqur berilib, kulishmoqda va juda jonli ijtimoiy uchrashuvdan zavqlanishayotgani aniq ko'rinib turibdi. Bu qiziqarli, yengil guruh dinamikasiga o'xshaydi.

Farqli o'laroq, ikkinchi rasmda atigi ikki do'st kofe ichayotgan, ancha samimiy muhit ta'kidlangan. Ular bir-biriga yaqinlashib, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ko'z bilan aloqa qilishmoqda, bu ularning chuqur, mazmunli muhokamada ekanligini yoki shaxsiy maslahat almashayotganini ko'rsatadi. Bu birinchi rasmga qaraganda ancha xotirjam va diqqat markazida bo'lgandek tuyuladi.

questions.prompt: Does having many friends affect a person’s psychology?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I have friends. I am happy.
questions.sampleA2: I have some friends. It is good. We play and talk. But sometimes I am sad.
questions.sampleB1: I think having many friends is good for you. For example, you can talk to them when you are sad. Also, it's fun to do things with a lot of people. However, sometimes it's hard to keep everyone happy. So, maybe it's better to have a few close friends.
questions.sampleB2: I'd say it definitely does, though it cuts both ways. On the plus side, a big circle gives you a real sense of belonging, and that can lift your mood and self-esteem. That said, keeping up with loads of people can be emotionally draining, and you might end up spreading yourself too thin. Honestly, I reckon it comes down to how deep those friendships really are.
questions.uzSampleA2: Mening bir nechta do'stlarim bor. Bu yaxshi. Biz o'ynaymiz va gaplashamiz. Lekin ba'zida men xafa bo'laman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, ko'p do'stlarga ega bo'lish siz uchun yaxshi.
Masalan, xafa bo'lganingizda ular bilan gaplasha olasiz. Shuningdek, ko'p odamlar bilan birga narsalar qilish qiziqarli.
Biroq, ba'zida hamma odamni xursand qilish qiyin. Shunday ekan, ehtimol, bir nechta yaqin do'stlarga ega bo'lish yaxshiroqdir.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Xo'sh, menimcha, ko'p do'stlarga ega bo'lish odamning psixologiyasiga albatta ta'sir qilishi mumkin. Bir tomondan, bu ijtimoiy aloqa va qo'llab-quvvatlash hissini kuchaytirishi mumkin, bu ruhiy farovonlik uchun juda muhim.
Biroq, bu doimiy ravishda muloqot qilish va bu munosabatlarni saqlab qolish uchun bosimni ham yaratishi mumkin. Bu stressga va o'zini haddan tashqari yuklanganlik hissi bilan bog'liq bo'lishiga olib kelishi mumkin.
Oxir oqibat, ta'sir shaxsning shaxsiyatiga va u o'zining ijtimoiy hayotini qanday boshqarishiga bog'liq bo'lishi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - Friends and psychology
idioms: quality over quantity - "sondan ko'ra sifat a'lo"
spread oneself too thin - "o'zini haddan tashqari ko'p ishlarga(yoki odamlarga) baxshida qilib yubormoq"
keep up appearances - "sir boy bermaslik (yaxshi ko'rinishga harakat qilmoq)"
sentenceStarters: "Having a large circle of friends can have a surprisingly complex effect on…" - "Katta do'stlar doirasiga ega bo'lish … ga hayratlanarli darajada murakkab ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin"
"On one hand, being part of a large network can provide…" - "Bir tomondan, katta tarmoqning bir qismi bo'lish … ni taqdim etishi mumkin"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Having a large circle of friends can have a surprisingly complex effect on a person's psychological state. On one hand, being part of a large network can provide a strong sense of belonging and social validation, which significantly boosts self-esteem and happiness.
On the other hand, maintaining numerous friendships can sometimes become emotionally exhausting. People might feel pressured to keep up appearances and, ironically, could still feel lonely if these connections are superficial. As they say, "quality is better than quantity."
Overall, while extroverts might thrive in large groups, the psychological benefit ultimately depends on the depth of the relationships rather than just the number of friends.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ko'p do'stga ega bo'lish insonning psixologik holatiga kutilmagan murakkab ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin. Bir tomondan, katta tarmoqning bir qismi bo'lish kuchli mansublik hissini va ijtimoiy tasdiqni ta'minlashi mumkin, bu esa o'z-o'zini qadrlash va baxtni sezilarli darajada oshiradi.

Boshqa tomondan, ko'plab do'stliklarni saqlash ba'zan hissiy jihatdan charchatishi mumkin. Odamlar o'zlarini tashqi ko'rinishni saqlashga majbur his qilishlari mumkin va, g'alati, agar bu aloqalar yuzaki bo'lsa, ular hali ham yolg'izlikni his qilishlari mumkin. Aytishlaricha, "sifat miqdordan yaxshiroq".

Umuman olganda, ekstrovertlar katta guruhlarda rivojlanishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, psixologik foyda oxir-oqibat do'stlarning sonidan ko'ra munosabatlarning chuqurligiga bog'liq.

questions.prompt: Why do people prefer having a heart-to-heart talk with one close friend?
questions.sampleA1: I like my friend. I talk to her. It is good.
questions.sampleA2: I talk to my friend. She is nice. I tell her my problems because she listens. And she helps me.
questions.sampleB1: I think people like talking to one friend because it's easier. You can tell them anything. For example, if you are sad, you can talk about it. In my opinion, it's better than talking to many people because it's more private. However, it depends on the problem.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I suppose it mainly comes down to trust. When it's just the two of you, it's far easier to open up and get things off your chest without feeling judged. You get their undivided attention, so the conversation can flow naturally. In a group, honestly, people tend to hold back because there's always that fear of being overheard or put on the spot.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga do'stim yoqadi. Men u bilan gaplashaman. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men do'stim bilan gaplashaman. U yaxshi. Men unga muammolarimni aytaman, chunki u meni eshitadi. Va u menga yordam beradi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Menimcha, odamlar bitta do'sti bilan gaplashishni yoqtirishadi, chunki bu osonroq. Ularga hamma narsani ayta olasiz. Masalan, agar siz xafa bo'lsangiz, bu haqda gaplasha olasiz. Mening fikrimcha, bu ko'p odamlar bilan gaplashgandan ko'ra yaxshiroq, chunki bu shaxsiyroq. Biroq, bu muammoga bog'liq.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Odamlar ko'pincha bir yaqin do'stiga dardlashni afzal ko'rishadi, chunki bu yerda yaqinlik va ishonch muhim rol o'ynaydi. Boshqa odam chin dildan tinglayotganini va sizning his-tuyg'ularingizga befarq emasligini bilsangiz, o'zingizni himoyasiz his qilish osonroq bo'ladi.
Bundan tashqari, yakkama-yakka suhbat chuqurroq aloqa va shaxsiy yordam berish imkonini yaratadi. Siz hukm qilinayotgan yoki fosh bo'layotganingizni his qilmasdan, muammolarga chuqur kirishingiz mumkin. Nihoyat, bir kishi bilan mazmunli suhbat tashkil qilish, guruh dinamikasini boshqarishdan ko'ra ko'pincha amaliyroqdir.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Heart-to-heart talks
idioms: a heart-to-heart - "dildan qilingan suhbat"
bare one's soul - "qalbini ochmoq (butun sirlarini aytib bermoq)"
get something off your chest - "yurakni bo'shatmoq (dardini aytib yengil tortmoq)"
sentenceStarters: "I believe people naturally gravitate towards one-on-one conversations when…" - "Men ishonamanki, odamlar … paytida tabiiy ravishda yakkama-yakka suhbatlarga moyil bo'lishadi"
"Furthermore, in a one-on-one setting, the listener can provide…" - "Qolaversa, yakkama-yakka sharoitda tinglovchi … taqdim etishi mumkin"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I believe people naturally gravitate towards one-on-one conversations when discussing sensitive topics because it creates a safe space. Psychologically, revealing vulnerabilities requires a high level of trust, which is much easier to establish with a single, close confidant.
Furthermore, in a one-on-one setting, the listener can provide their undivided attention. There is no fear of judgment from a crowd, and the conversation can flow more organically. It's much easier to truly open up to one person.
Ultimately, having a "heart-to-heart" is about seeking deep understanding, empathy, and tailored advice, which large group dynamics simply cannot offer. It allows individuals to bare their souls comfortably.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Menimcha, odamlar sezgir mavzularni muhokama qilishda tabiiy ravishda yuzma-yuz suhbatlarga intilishadi, chunki bu xavfsiz muhit yaratadi. Psixologik nuqtai nazardan, zaif tomonlarni ochish yuqori darajadagi ishonchni talab qiladi, uni bitta yaqin sirdosh bilan o'rnatish ancha oson.

Bundan tashqari, yuzma-yuz muhitda tinglovchi o'zining to'liq e'tiborini qaratishi mumkin. Olomon tomonidan hukm qilinish qo'rquvi yo'q va suhbat yanada tabiiy ravishda davom etishi mumkin. Bir insonga chin dildan ochilish ancha oson.

Oxir oqibat, "dildan suhbat" chuqur tushunish, hamdardlik va moslashtirilgan maslahat izlashdan iborat bo'lib, buni katta guruh dinamikasi oddiygina taklif qila olmaydi. Bu odamlarga o'z qalbini qulay tarzda ochishga imkon beradi.

questions.prompt: Can you describe a time when you felt proud of yourself?
questions.sampleA1: I happy when I play football. I win. I good.
questions.sampleA2: I proud when I finished school. It was hard, but I did it. And my family was happy too.
questions.sampleB1: I felt really proud when I passed my driving test. I was nervous, but I studied a lot. I think it's a big achievement because now I have more freedom. Also, my parents were very happy.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so a time I felt genuinely proud of myself... the one that really springs to mind is when I organised a charity fundraiser at my old college. To be honest, I'd never taken on anything that big before, and at the start I was completely out of my depth. I had to track down sponsors, round up volunteers, and basically promote the whole thing from scratch. There were loads of moments where it nearly fell apart — people dropped out, the venue messed us around — and I honestly thought about giving up. But I stuck with it, and on the day everything came together. We ended up raising a fair bit for the local hospital, and that gave me this incredible sense of accomplishment. Watching everyone turn up and enjoy the day made all those sleepless nights completely worth it. As for why people feel proud of their achievements, I suppose it's because success is tangible proof that all your hard work has actually paid off. When you've poured your heart into something and it comes good, it validates the sacrifices you made. The thing is, it also ties into a basic human need to feel competent and recognised. And as for how success shapes motivation — well, in my experience it creates a real knock-on effect. Once you've pulled off one thing, you start believing you can take on even bigger challenges. Basically, success breeds success; each little win builds your confidence and spurs you on to keep raising the bar. It's honestly one of the most rewarding feelings there is.

bulletPoints: Can you describe a time when you felt proud of yourself?
Why do people feel proud of their achievements?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A time I felt proud:
I was immensely proud of myself last year when I successfully organized a local charity marathon. I was entirely responsible for finding sponsors, coordinating volunteers, and marketing the event. Despite numerous logistical nightmares, we ultimately raised a substantial amount of money. Seeing the runners cross the finish line gave me an unparalleled sense of accomplishment.
Why people feel proud of achievements:
People naturally feel proud of their achievements because it validates their hard work and perseverance. It provides tangible proof that their sacrifices were not in vain. Experiencing a sense of victory satisfies a core human psychological need for competence and recognition, showing that we are capable of overcoming challenges.
How success influences motivation:
Success profoundly influences motivation by creating a positive feedback loop. When you achieve a goal, the dopamine release acts as a powerful catalyst to set even higher targets. Essentially, "success breeds success"; it builds the self-efficacy required to tackle future projects with unwavering determination and unshakeable confidence.

O'tgan yili mahalliy xayriya marafonini muvaffaqiyatli tashkil qilganimda o'zimdan juda faxrlangan edim. Men homiylarni topish, ko'ngillilarni muvofiqlashtirish va tadbirni marketing qilish uchun to'liq mas'ul edim. Ko'plab logistik muammolarga qaramay, biz oxir-oqibatda katta miqdorda pul yig'dik. Yuguruvchilarning finish chizig'ini kesib o'tganini ko'rish menga misli ko'rilmagan yutuq tuyg'usini berdi.

Nima uchun odamlar yutuqlardan faxrlanadi:

Odamlar o'z yutuqlaridan tabiiy ravishda faxrlanadilar, chunki bu ularning mashaqqatli mehnati va qat'iyatini tasdiqlaydi. Bu ularning qurbonliklari behuda ketmaganligining aniq dalilini beradi. G'alaba tuyg'usini his qilish, bizning qiyinchiliklarni yengishga qodirligimizni ko'rsatib, insonning asosiy psixologik ehtiyojini - kompetentlik va e'tirofni qondiradi.

Muvaffaqiyat motivatsiyaga qanday ta'sir qiladi:

Muvaffaqiyat ijobiy teskari aloqa zanjirini yaratish orqali motivatsiyaga chuqur ta'sir qiladi. Maqsadga erishganingizda, dopaminning ajralishi yanada yuqori maqsadlarni qo'yish uchun kuchli katalizator vazifasini bajaradi. Aslida, "muvaffaqiyat muvaffaqiyatni keltirib chiqaradi"; u kelajakdagi loyihalarni qat'iy azm va qat'iy ishonch bilan hal qilish uchun zarur bo'lgan o'z-o'ziga ishonchni shakllantiradi.

questions.prompt: Fast food restaurants should display calorie counts.
questions.sampleA2: I think yes. It is good to see calories. Because maybe food is very fat. And I don't want fat.
questions.sampleB1: I think it's a good idea to show calories in fast food. It helps people to know what they are eating. For example, if you want to lose weight, you can choose something with fewer calories. However, some people might not care about the numbers, so it might not work for everyone.
questions.sampleB2: This is a really interesting one, and I can genuinely see both sides of it. On the one hand, the people in favour make a solid point about transparency. If calorie counts are right there on the menu, customers can make far more informed choices about what they're eating. It might nudge someone towards a healthier option, and over time, that kind of awareness could help bring down obesity rates, which are honestly spiralling out of control in a lot of countries. So from a public-health angle, it makes a lot of sense. That said, the other camp raises some fair concerns too. The thing is, when someone's craving a burger, a number on the wall probably isn't going to put them off — habit tends to win out over logic. On top of that, for people who struggle with eating disorders, seeing calories everywhere can be genuinely triggering and pile on the anxiety. And there's another catch: calories only tell half the story. A so-called low-calorie meal might still be loaded with sugar and additives, so it can be a bit misleading. Personally, I'm broadly in favour, but I don't think it's a silver bullet. To my mind, the numbers are a useful starting point, but they need to go hand in hand with proper nutritional education. At the end of the day, teaching people what actually makes up a healthy meal would do far more good than just slapping figures on a menu and expecting the problem to fix itself.

against: Might not significantly affect eating habits
Can create anxiety around food choices
Focuses too much on calorie count, not on nutritional value

questions.sampleAnswer:
The proposal that fast food restaurants should mandatorily display calorie counts has sparked a vigorous debate. Supporters strongly argue that transparency is crucial for public health. By clearly seeing the caloric impact, customers can make informed dietary choices. Moreover, this visual reminder subconsciously encourages healthier habits and could potentially play a vital role in curbing rising global obesity rates.
Conversely, opponents remain highly skeptical about its efficacy. They point out that habit overrides logic; a hungry person craving a burger will likely ignore the numbers anyway. Furthermore, displaying these figures can trigger severe anxiety for individuals with eating disorders. Most importantly, critics argue it misleadingly focuses entirely on calorie intake rather than actual nutritional value—a low-calorie item might still be packed with unhealthy chemicals.
In conclusion, while the intention behind displaying calories is noble, it is not a "silver bullet." True public health improvements require comprehensive nutritional education rather than simply plastering numbers on a menu.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Tez ovqatlanish restoranlari kaloriya miqdorini majburiy ravishda ko'rsatishi kerakligi haqidagi taklif qizg'in bahslarga sabab bo'ldi. Tarafdorlar shaffoflik jamoat salomatligi uchun juda muhim ekanligini qat'iy ta'kidlashadi. Kaloriya ta'sirini aniq ko'rish orqali mijozlar oqilona ovqatlanish tanlovini amalga oshirishlari mumkin. Bundan tashqari, bu vizual eslatma ongsiz ravishda sog'lom odatlarni rag'batlantiradi va global semizlik darajasining oshishini to'xtatishda muhim rol o'ynashi mumkin.

Aksincha, qarshilar uning samaradorligiga nisbatan juda shubha bilan qarashadi. Ular odat mantiqdan ustun turishini ta'kidlashadi; burgerga chanqagan och odam, ehtimol, raqamlarga e'tibor bermaydi. Bundan tashqari, bu raqamlarni ko'rsatish ovqatlanish buzilishlari bo'lgan shaxslar uchun kuchli xavotirni keltirib chiqarishi mumkin. Eng muhimi, tanqidchilarning ta'kidlashicha, u haqiqiy ozuqaviy qiymatdan ko'ra, faqat kaloriya iste'moliga noto'g'ri e'tibor qaratadi - kam kaloriyali mahsulot hali ham zararli kimyoviy moddalar bilan to'ldirilgan bo'lishi mumkin.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, kaloriyalarni ko'rsatishdan maqsad ezgu bo'lsa-da, bu "barcha dardga davo" emas. Haqiqiy jamoat salomatligini yaxshilash menyuga shunchaki raqamlarni yopishtirishdan ko'ra, har tomonlama oziqlanish bo'yicha ta'limni talab qiladi.
